entries.title: Ruth 3:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rest - A life of rest, and comfort, and safety, under the care of a good husband.

entries.title: Ruth 3:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Threshing - floor - Which was in a place covered at the top, but open elsewhere, whither Ruth might easily come. And this work of winnowing corn was usually ended with a feast.

entries.title: Ruth 3:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Raiment - Thy best raiment. Known - In so familiar a way, as thou mayest do hereafter.

entries.title: Ruth 3:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Uncover his feet - Remove the clothes that were upon his feet; thereby to awaken him. Will tell thee - What course thou shalt take to obtain that marriage which belongs unto thee.

entries.title: Ruth 3:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: At midnight - He did not discover her sooner.

entries.title: Ruth 3:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Spread thy Skirt - That is, take me to be thy wife, and perform the duty of an husband to me.

entries.title: Ruth 3:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shewed kindness - Both to thy deceased husband, the continuance of whose name and memory thou seekest; and to thy mother - in - law, whose commands thou hast punctually obeyed. Followedst not - To seek thy marriage here, or in thy own country, as thou wouldst have done if thou hadst not preferred obedience to God's command, before pleasing thyself.

entries.title: Ruth 3:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Perform, &100. - Take thee to wife, to raise up seed to his brother. Bishop Hall sums up the matter thus. "Boaz, instead of touching her as a wanton, blesseth her as a father, encourages her as a friend, promises her as a kinsman, rewards her as a patron, and sends her away laden with hopes and gifts, no less chast, but more happy than she came. O admirable temperance, worthy the progenitor of him, in whose lips and heart there was no guile!"

entries.title: Ruth 3:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Let it not, &100. - He takes care to preserve not only his conscience towards God, but his reputation, and hers also, among men.

entries.title: Ruth 3:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Who art thou? - This is not a question of doubting, but of wonder, as if she had said, Art thou in very deed my daughter? I can hardly believe it. How camest thou hither in this manner, and thus early?
